opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
The lamp of the body is the eye. If the eye is sound, your whole body will be filled with light, but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be in darkness. And if the light in you is darkness, how great will be the darkness. I am slightly stumped on this because sound is good, and bad is bad, but sound is also many other things. Why the distinction?

Jesus could have said "good eye" and "bad eye," but He didn't. The distinction matters. A "good" eye would primarily describe moral behavior. A "sound" eye describes condition and function. Think about it this way: a good eye might mean an eye that chooses good things, while a sound eye means an eye that works properly and sees reality accurately. Jesus is speaking less about morality and more about perception. The issue is not whether the eye is virtuous but whether it is healthy enough to receive light.

If I have a diseased eye, I may sincerely believe I am seeing correctly while everything is distorted. The problem is not my intentions; it is the condition of my vision. This is why many translations use healthy eye and unhealthy eye, sound eye and bad eye, clear eye and diseased eye. There is another layer. In Jewish thought, a "good eye" and an "evil eye" were common expressions. A "good eye" often meant generosity, while an "evil eye" meant envy, greed, or selfishness. Jesus may be drawing on that imagery, especially since He is discussing treasure and money in the surrounding verses.

But even there, the focus is not simply moral goodness. A generous person sees abundance and trusts God. A greedy person sees scarcity and becomes consumed by possessions. Their entire way of seeing the world is different. So "sound" is actually more precise than "good." A sound eye is healthy, undivided, clear, functioning as designed, and able to receive light. A bad eye is diseased, distorted, divided, and unable to receive light properly.

What strikes me is that Jesus is describing something we all experience. Two people can look at the exact same event and see completely different realities because the "eye" through which they are viewing it is different. One sees grace, opportunity, and God's presence. The other sees only threat, loss, and resentment. The question becomes: Is my spiritual vision healthy enough to recognize the light when it is right in front of me? That is a deeper question than simply, "Am I being good?" It is asking whether the instrument by which you perceive God and reality is functioning as it was created to function.

Jesus, I ask from the depths of my heart to heal my eye and restore my vision, that I may see more clearly and more abundantly. Remove the blindness of judgment, the narrowness of selfishness, and anything that distorts the truth. Grant me eyes filled with compassion, generosity, mercy, and understanding, so that I may see others as You see them and recognize Your light wherever it shines. May my vision be sound, my heart undivided, and my whole being filled with Your light. Amen.
